## Grading {#grading}

Weights as announced in class in 2018. The full breakdown was published on the original course page and is not reproduced here.

```{=html}
<table class="t" data-quarto-disable-processing="true">
<thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Weight</th><th>How</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><th>Quizzes</th><td class="big">10%</td><td>Each quiz is worth 10%. See <a href="#quizzes">Quizzes</a>.</td></tr>
<tr><th>Project</th><td class="big">8%</td><td>Raised from 5% to 8% during the semester, with the 3% taken from homework. See <a href="#project">Project</a>.</td></tr>
<tr><th>Homework</th><td class="big">–</td><td>Four individual homework sets, typed and submitted as a PDF. See <a href="assignments.html">Homework</a>.</td></tr>
<tr><th>Labs</th><td class="big">–</td><td>Lab sheets and a lab quiz. See <a href="labs.html">Labs</a>.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
```

Homework is graded with a least count of 0.5 marks. Plagiarism is not tolerated, and all references must be cited in IEEE format.

:::

::: {.two .rule-top}

## Project {#project}

- Project ideas are collected in the [course project ideas spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eVVmBrCTXHa6XhfewG2S9_if11Ija0s_cNMBp5NMbww/edit?usp=sharing).
- Projects are shown in class as a demo or a video.
- The project counts for 8% (raised from 5% during the semester).
- Projects were graded in rounds: the second round on 12 and 16 November, the third and final round on 19 and 23 November.

:::
